newsitem.title: USA: Study shows DC gets "powerful kick" from tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Study shows DC gets "powerful kick" from tax cut.

text.p: A key U.S. senator said Wednesday that a new study shows his tax cut proposal for the District of Columbia would give both the city and regional economy a "powerful kick."

Sen. Sam Brownback, a Republican for Kansas, said the new study by Wharton Forecasting Associates shows that his D.C. Economic Recovery Act would cost the federal Treasury far less than anticipated. Brownback chairs the Senate Governmental Affairs subcommittee on D.C.

The bill would tax D.C. residents at a single 15 percent rate for all income earned within the metropolitan area, allow first-time homebuyers a $5,000 tax credit and eliminate capital gains city-wide.
Wharton economists found that while the bill would trigger roughly $1.1 billion in lost revenues to the federal government, those losses would be offset by a number of gains.

For instance, by 2002, disposable income in the region would increase by $10.7 billion or 7.6 percent as a result of the bill, the study says. By 2007, the figure grows to $19.5 billion or 11.7 percent, Wharton says.
Employment would jump by 101,700 or 3.7 percent by 2002 and 112,600 or 3.8 percent by 2007, Wharton says.
